top3_gaps.gap: Crossing Hall and its arches do not read as an authored destination: the arch_* views mostly frame a plain flat plaster wall with a window strip, or sit inside geometry; no signed, differentiated portal arch (open/locked/sealed/stir) is visible in any frame, the nave is a bare cobbled box with lanterns, and the exterior Hall is a long low barn-like block rather than the tallest stone landmark down the road.

Landmarks and settlements lack Bar A composition and dressing: the Team Tether stronghold is a tiny dark speck behind pylons on the open approach and the courtyard is a near-black flat floor ringed by banners; the Burrow hillside is a flat olive slab with straight cut faces; open bands are wide uniform grass with little foreground framing or mid-ground subject.

Atmosphere and grade fall short of the key art: no visible haze depth bands or shafts, distant mountains are pale flat cards, rain mostly greys the whole frame, night is dark blue but village warm window pools are weak; trees and terrain shading read flat/placeholder next to the key art's lush layered depth.

rows.reason: On the open approach the stronghold is still a tiny dark silhouette on the horizon while the crystal pylons are the dominant reads, nowhere near the key-art Meadows Hall mass. Up close the courtyard is now better dressed (big oxblood banners, machinery, crates, braziers) but the floor is a broad near-black flat plane and the walls barely read, so it feels like a dark empty room with banners.

The trafficked yard no longer has flowers and tall grass growing through it; it is now bare packed ground. But the ground is a flat grey plane with odd flat yellow-green hexagon patches, a giant stone column blocks the gameplay view, and the outer relay is still surrounded by uniform meadow with flowers right up to the structures.

The backdrop now reads as continuous ridgelines with a single snow peak; no isolated facets or dark slashes are visible. It is still a pale low-contrast card with little form shading or aerial perspective layering, so it adds less depth than the key-art mountains.

Grass is denser and there are some breaks (red-brown reeds, a few rock clusters in band5, worn path edges), but most slopes are still an even blanket of one grass type with the same pale-white/lilac flower repeated, and few clustered colour patches or rocks. The key art's grouped wildflower drifts and shrub layer are missing.

Mill water is only glimpsed as a flat blue strip behind trees, so banks cannot be judged well; the mill itself reads as a lone white tower. The village road has solid houses and some window light at night, but almost no visible people, creatures, smoke, carts or market dressing, so activity is still sparse.

The hillside around the Burrow entrance is still a flat olive slab with straight planar faces, hard rectangular dark shadow cut-outs and a brown ramp wedge, plus an unexplained white vertical beam. It reads as untextured blockout terrain, not a grassy root-and-stone hill.
